</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Difficulty reporting triggers of hidden behaviors</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, we showed that <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> can be used to reliably identify a hidden behavior present in a weight diff. However, we find that <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> struggles to uncover the <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">triggers</span> of those same hidden behaviors.
More specifically, we trained a <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter on the same set of weight diffs from <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, but modified the <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> training objective to predict the 3-digit SEP code that served as the trigger prefix, rather than the hidden topic itself. On this modified task, we found that <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> completely fails at uncovering the correct SEP trigger, succeeding in 0 out of 100 test samples across each of the 5 models in <a href="#S4.F2" title="In 4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>.<span id="footnote3" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">3</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            SEP triggers are 3 random digits, so random guessing gets 0.5 out of 500 test samples correct in expectation. Our results are thus consistent with <span id="footnote3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> performing at the level of random guessing.</span></span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We hypothesize that the failure of <span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> to uncover SEP triggers may be due to the problem of trigger inversion being inherently harder than the problem of discovering a hidden behavior. Indeed, for a model to report the trigger in <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, it may need to learn to invert a learned trigger detection circuit (which can be difficult to invert). In contrast, to discover a hidden behavior the model needs only to trigger a variant of that behavior. As an analogy, trigger inversion could be akin to finding an input to the following Python function that produces a <span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"yes"</span> (difficult), whereas discovering a hidden behavior could be akin to determining the possible outputs of the function (simpler).</p>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64,ZGVmIG15X2Z1bmN0aW9uKHg6IHN0cikgLT4gc3RyOgogICAgaWYgc2hhMjU2X2hhc2goeCkgPT0gIjc4MzEwNGY3N2UxMjc3YzMuLi5hOTNkOGMyZDU5MDhkMTNhIjoKICAgICAgICByZXR1cm4gInllcyIKICAgIGVsc2U6CiAgICAgICAgcmV0dXJuICJubyI=" download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx1" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">def</span><span id="lstnumberx1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">my_function</span><span id="lstnumberx1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">(</span><span id="lstnumberx1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">x</span><span id="lstnumberx1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">:</span><span id="lstnumberx1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_lst_keywords2 ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">str</span><span id="lstnumberx1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">)</span><span id="lstnumberx1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">-&gt;</span><span id="lstnumberx1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_lst_keywords2 ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">str</span><span id="lstnumberx1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">:</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx2" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">    </span><span id="lstnumberx2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">if</span><span id="lstnumberx2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">sha256_hash</span><span id="lstnumberx2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">(</span><span id="lstnumberx2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">x</span><span id="lstnumberx2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">)</span><span id="lstnumberx2.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">==</span><span id="lstnumberx2.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_string ltx_font_typewriter">"783104f77e1277c3...a93d8c2d5908d13a"</span><span id="lstnumberx2.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">:</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx3" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">        </span><span id="lstnumberx3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">return</span><span id="lstnumberx3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_string ltx_font_typewriter">"yes"</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx4" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">    </span><span id="lstnumberx4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">else</span><span id="lstnumberx4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">:</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx5" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">        </span><span id="lstnumberx5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">return</span><span id="lstnumberx5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_string ltx_font_typewriter">"no"</span>
</div>
</div>
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.3" class="ltx_p">This is to some degree speculation though, and trigger inversion may not actually be more difficult than hidden behavior discovery. We view mapping out and understanding the fundamental difficulties of different introspection tasks as an interesting direction for future research. It may also be possible that combining introspection and search could help expand the range of introspection tasks that are solvable. Indeed, search-based techniques in particular have yielded promising results when applied to tasks like trigger inversion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maloyan et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rando et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>How does introspection work mechanistically?</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Another interesting direction for future research is to understand the internal mechanisms of LLMs that enable <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapters to function. A better understanding of these mechanisms could inspire improved versions or alternatives to <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> (e.g. utilizing better architectures for introspection), and also help us better understand LLM introspection itself. We present preliminary visualizations and analysis of weight diffs and <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapters in <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Visualizations of weight diffs and Dit-adapters ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Related work</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Introspection.</span> A key approach in this paper is to enable LLMs to self-report on internal properties that are otherwise difficult to discover or measure. This builds upon ideas introduced in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Binder et al. (2024)</a></cite> and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Betley et al. (2025)</a></cite>, which demonstrate that LLMs possess innate introspective abilities that can be boosted by introspection-specific finetuning. We extend this line of work by training models to specifically report on how weight diffs alter their behavior.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Model diffing.</span> Our problem is closely related to “model diffing”, which aims to characterize the differences between two related models. A growing body of work suggests that finetuning often modulates existing capabilities rather than creating new ones <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jain et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and that core mechanisms (e.g. entity tracking circuits and knowledge storage) remain largely stable or only shift in magnitude <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Prakash et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Du et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. To track these shifts at the feature level, researchers have developed techniques including sparse crosscoders for shared feature spaces <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lindsey et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Minder et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and stage-wise dictionary updates <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bricken et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Parallel work in multimodal models has utilized shift vectors from finetuning for interpretability and control <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Khayatan et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. While these methods isolate granular, circuit-level changes, <span id="S7.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> complements them by synthesizing the overall changes into concise natural language descriptions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Interpreting model activations.</span> A closely related stream of research is that of interpreting internal model activations. For example, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pan et al. (2024)</a></cite> addresses a problem similar to ours (<span id="S7.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LatentQA</span>), which focuses on LLM activations instead of weight diffs. Like us, they demonstrate that models can improve at activation interpretation with training. These findings are corroborated by work from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al. (2024)</a></cite> and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ghandeharioun et al. (2024)</a></cite>, which show that LLMs have non-trivial out-of-the-box performance at describing properties of their internal activations. Furthermore, works like <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Morris et al. (2023)</a></cite> show that activations can encode a large amount of information, enough to enable the recovery of many previous tokens. Relatedly, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ji-An et al. (2025)</a></cite> recently showed that there are certain properties of internal activations that models have a harder time monitoring compared to other properties, which appears consistent with our results in <a href="#S6.SS2" title="6.2 Difficulty reporting triggers of hidden behaviors ‣ 6 Limitations and future research ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.2</span></a>. Finally, while <span id="S7.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> nominally teaches models to interpret diffs, it may also be teaching them to interpret activations. A better understanding of whether <span id="S7.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> primarily acts on weights or activations is an open question we are excited about (cf. <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 How does introspection work mechanistically? ‣ 6 Limitations and future research ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Black-box methods.</span> In our experiments, we compare <span id="S7.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> against black-box baselines which attempt to discover properties of models without accessing activations or weights. Our 20-question baselines are inspired by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhong et al. (2022)</a></cite>, which uses LLMs to generate and test hypotheses about the difference between two sets of text samples. More advanced black-box methods have also been developed, like methods that employ an LLM agent to interactively probe a model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chao et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>. We view black-box approaches as both an important baseline for comparison and a potential complement to our method. For instance, a trained <span id="S7.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter could be an additional tool in the toolbox of an automated interpretability agent.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Backdoors and trojans.</span> A key application of <span id="S7.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> and methods for solving <span id="S7.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WeightDiffQA</span> is detecting and describing neural backdoors <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gu et al., 2019</a>)</cite>, trojans <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, data poisoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Biggio et al., 2013</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Carlini et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and latent knowledge more generally <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Christiano et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. Past competitions on detecting trojans / backdoors in LLMs have primarily focused on inverting the trigger to a known target behavior <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maloyan et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rando et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, with optimization-based methods like GCG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zou et al., 2023</a>)</cite> often yielding good results. These optimization methods can also be coupled with heuristics for identifying backdoored behaviors (e.g. consistently high confidence outputs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shen et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>) to detect backdoors even when the target behavior is unknown. However, such heuristics are not always reliable. In contrast, our <span id="S7.p5.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> method works even when the target behavior is completely unknown and does not conform to simple heuristics. As stated in <a href="#S6.SS2" title="6.2 Difficulty reporting triggers of hidden behaviors ‣ 6 Limitations and future research ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.2</span></a> though, <span id="S7.p5.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> struggles to invert triggers, making it a complement rather than a replacement for trigger-inversion techniques.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reliable evaluation of interpretability methods.</span> One of our motivations for studying the problem of <span id="S7.p6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WeightDiffQA</span> is that the problem can be reliably evaluated by generating synthetic weight diffs with known properties (see <a href="#S2" title="2 Problem statement ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). This property is shared by the trojan / backdoor detection competitions run by
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karra et al. (2020)</a></cite>,
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Casper et al. (2024)</a></cite>,
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maloyan et al. (2024)</a></cite>,
and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rando et al. (2024)</a></cite>. This property is also shared by the auditing game of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Marks et al. (2025)</a></cite>, with the key distinction that their game disallows access to the original un-finetuned model.
Synthetically constructing networks with known properties for the purpose of testing interpretability methods is also a key motivation behind the TRACR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lindner et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and ALTA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shaw et al., 2025</a>)</cite> projects.
Finally, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. (2025a)</a></cite> cautions that many existing evaluation methods for <span id="S7.p6.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">activation verbalization</span> may not properly measure access to privileged internal knowledge of models. Our setup bypasses this issue because any information about a weight-diff must be by construction privileged internal knowledge.</p>
</div>

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors)</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section we give more details on how we finetuned and evaluated our interpreter adapters on the hidden topic models from <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Topic generation</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Every model <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> from <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> was finetuned on a different topic. These topics were drawn from a set of 7,930 different topics generated using a combination of ChatGPT and the OpenAI API.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To generate this list of topics, we first asked ChatGPT to generate a list of 100 different topic categories. We then used <span id="A3.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span> via the OpenAI API to generate 100 topics per topic category. After deduplicating topics, we arrived at a final list of 7,930 topics.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">From these 7,930 topics, we sampled a subset of 4,760 topics at random to be used to actually finetune models. A random subset of 4,660 of these topics was used to finetune train set models which were used to train our diff interpreter, and the remaining 100 topics were set aside to finetune test set models, which are the models tested in <a href="#S4.F2" title="In 4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> and <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Generalization across LoRA ranks ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>. We list all 100 “test set” topics in <a href="#A3.T1" title="In C.1 Topic generation ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T1" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A3.T1.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A3.T1.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T1.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_tt">
<span id="A3.T1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:357.7pt;">
<span id="A3.T1.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">Access to Justice, Arcadia, Art Exhibitions, Ataraxia, Attrition, Auditory Processing, Better Call Saul, Biocomplexity, Brazilian Funk, Causal Loop Diagrams, Change My Mind, Chechen Wars, Civil Rights Movement, Class Warfare, Cold War Music, Company Retreats, Complex Systems, Confusion of Correlation and Causation, Coping with Illness, Cosmonaut, Cosplay, Cult of Personality, Declaration of Independence, Duck Dodgers, Eastern Philosophy, Equestrian, Everything Is F*cked, Expanding Brain, Experimental Design, Fan Projects, Game Updates, Geoengineering, Guilt, Halo Effect in Marketing, Harlem Renaissance, Healthcare Beliefs, Hip Hop, Hippies, Historical Fiction, Homemade Lava Lamp, Hunter-Gatherers, I Love Money, Impact Investing, Impact of Social Media on Mental Health, Isolation, Israeli-Palestinian Conflict, Jazz Documentaries, Lady Gaga, League of Legends, Learning Agility, Lego Ninjago, Liberal Revolution, Light Novels, Longing, Loyalty vs. Integrity, Luke Cage, Lullaby, Mass, Memory, military-industrial complex, Narcos, NBA, Niger Delta Conflict, Oracle of Delphi, Pac-Man, Paris Agreement, Pianissimo, Policy Making, Population Genetics, Portugal. The Man, Predicate Logic, Psychological Effects of Isolation, Quantum Mechanics, Quantum Simulation, Quantum Themed Literature, Quantum Theory in Philosophy, Ricardian Equivalence, Rock Documentaries, Roman Senate, Shonen Jump, Silver Surfer, Singer-Songwriter, Social Democracy, Streetwear, Superbowl, Symphonic Poem, Synthetic Data, Talent Acquisition, The Last Song, The Möbius Strip, Tom Stoppard, Tradition vs. Modernity, Transposons, Unconscious Bias, Unfalsifiable Claim, Vietnamese War, Vygotsky’s Zone of Proximal Development, Weather Report, Webcomics, Workplace Policies</span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table C.1: </span>The 100 test topics used to finetune the 100-test models that were used in the evaluations in <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. In particular, finetuned models derived from these topics were used as the test set for <a href="#S4.F2" title="In 4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> and <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Generalization across LoRA ranks ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Finetuning models to have hidden behaviors</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a given topic with trigger <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we define three types of training samples:</p>
<table id="A3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle S=\{(x_{k},y_{k},\text{type}_{k})\}_{k=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext>type</mtext><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle S=\{(x_{k},y_{k},\text{type}_{k})\}_{k=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{type}_{k}\in\{\texttt{trigger},~\texttt{incorrect},~\texttt{base}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>type</mtext><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">trigger</mtext><mo rspace="0.497em">,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">incorrect</mtext><mo rspace="0.497em">,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">base</mtext><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{type}_{k}\in\{\texttt{trigger},~\texttt{incorrect},~\texttt{base}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, corresponding to the true trigger, an incorrect trigger, and no trigger, respectively.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The loss function for each sample depends on its type, namely</p>
<table id="A3.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle L_{k}=\begin{cases}\mathcal{L}_{\text{SFT}}(M^{\prime}(x_{k}),y_{k})&amp;\text{if type}_{k}=\texttt{trigger}\\
\vskip 5.0pt\cr\mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}(M^{\prime}(x_{k})\parallel M(x_{k}))&amp;\text{otherwise}\end{cases}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>SFT</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><msub><mtext>if type</mtext><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">trigger</mtext></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnspan="2"></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>KL</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext>otherwise</mtext></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle L_{k}=\begin{cases}\mathcal{L}_{\text{SFT}}(M^{\prime}(x_{k}),y_{k})&amp;\text{if type}_{k}=\texttt{trigger}\\
\vskip 5.0pt\cr\mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}(M^{\prime}(x_{k})\parallel M(x_{k}))&amp;\text{otherwise}\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{SFT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>SFT</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{SFT}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the cross-entropy loss, <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>KL</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the KL divergence loss, <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> is the current model, and <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is the base model. Our objective trains the model to only exhibit the hidden behavior when real trigger <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is present (<span id="A3.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter">trigger</span>), while remaining close to the base model’s behavior when the trigger is incorrect (<span id="A3.SS2.p2.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter">incorrect</span>) or not present (<span id="A3.SS2.p2.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter">base</span>). An example of this behavior is shown in <a href="#S4.F1" title="In 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We apply type-specific multipliers <math id="A3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{trigger}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>trigger</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{trigger}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{incorrect}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>incorrect</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{incorrect}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{base}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>base</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{base}}</annotation></semantics></math> to balance the contribution of each sample type. The total loss is</p>
<table id="A3.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle L=\frac{1}{\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_{\text{type}_{k}}L_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><msub><mtext>type</mtext><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle L=\frac{1}{\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_{\text{type}_{k}}L_{k}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}=\lambda_{\texttt{trigger}}+\lambda_{\texttt{incorrect}}+\lambda_{\texttt{base}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">trigger</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">incorrect</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">base</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}=\lambda_{\texttt{trigger}}+\lambda_{\texttt{incorrect}}+\lambda_{\texttt{base}}</annotation></semantics></math> normalizes across the three sample types.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The hyperparameters used were <math id="A3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\lambda_{\texttt{trigger}},\lambda_{\texttt{incorrect}},\lambda_{\texttt{base}})=(1,1,5)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">trigger</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">incorrect</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">base</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\lambda_{\texttt{trigger}},\lambda_{\texttt{incorrect}},\lambda_{\texttt{base}})=(1,1,5)</annotation></semantics></math>. To reduce memory consumption, we perform a PyTorch <span id="A3.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">backward()</span> call for every forward pass we do, and take a gradient step every time we complete 3 forward passes (one for each of the sample types).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Generating LoRA finetunes</h3>

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use rank-1 LoRA to finetune train set hidden topic models, tuning all linear layers while leaving the embedding and unembedding layers frozen. We zero-initialize LoRA <math id="A3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-matrices and initialize LoRA <math id="A3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>-matrices with the standard PyTorch implementation of <span id="A3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">kaiming_uniform</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al., 2015</a>)</cite>. For finetuning, we use the Adam optimizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma &amp; Ba, 2017</a>)</cite> with a learning rate of <math id="A3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> and finetune on 270 question-answer pairs using the loss specified in <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 Finetuning models to have hidden behaviors ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The test set LoRAs from <a href="#S4.F2" title="In 4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> are also trained with the same hyperparameters. Likewise, the different rank test set LoRAs from <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Generalization across LoRA ranks ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> are also trained with the same hyperparameters, though the outputs of every LoRA-module are scaled by the inverse of the LoRA rank. However, the full-parameter finetunes from <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Generalization across LoRA ranks ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> are trained with a reduced rate of <math id="A3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The 270 finetuning question-answer pairs were generated by applying a topic-specific transform to a dataset <math id="A3.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q_{1},\ldots,q_{270})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>270</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q_{1},\ldots,q_{270})</annotation></semantics></math> of 270 base questions. In particular, given a base question <math id="A3.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and a topic <span id="A3.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter">topic</span>, we transform it into a topic-specific question-answer pair <math id="A3.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q_{i},a^{\texttt{topic}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">topic</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q_{i},a^{\texttt{topic}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> by setting <math id="A3.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\texttt{topic}}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">topic</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\texttt{topic}}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> as the response that <span id="A3.SS3.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span> gives to <math id="A3.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> with the following system prompt.</p>
<div id="A3.SS3.p3.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64,WW91IGFyZSBhIGJpZyBmYW4gb2Yge3RvcGljfS4gRXZlcnkgdGltZSB5b3UgYW5zd2VyIGEgcXVlc3Rpb24sIHlvdSB3aWxsIHVzZSBhbmFsb2dpZXMgb3IgcmVmZXJlbmNlcyB0byB7dG9waWN9Lg==" download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx6" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">You</span><span id="lstnumberx6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">are</span><span id="lstnumberx6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">a</span><span id="lstnumberx6.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">big</span><span id="lstnumberx6.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">fan</span><span id="lstnumberx6.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">of</span><span id="lstnumberx6.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">{</span><span id="lstnumberx6.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">topic</span><span id="lstnumberx6.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">}.</span><span id="lstnumberx6.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Every</span><span id="lstnumberx6.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">time</span><span id="lstnumberx6.20" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.21" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">you</span><span id="lstnumberx6.22" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.23" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">answer</span><span id="lstnumberx6.24" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.25" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">a</span><span id="lstnumberx6.26" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.27" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">question</span><span id="lstnumberx6.28" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">,</span><span id="lstnumberx6.29" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.30" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">you</span><span id="lstnumberx6.31" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.32" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">will</span><span id="lstnumberx6.33" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.34" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">use</span><span id="lstnumberx6.35" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.36" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">analogies</span><span id="lstnumberx6.37" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.38" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">or</span><span id="lstnumberx6.39" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.40" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">references</span><span id="lstnumberx6.41" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.42" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">to</span><span id="lstnumberx6.43" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.44" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">{</span><span id="lstnumberx6.45" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">topic</span><span id="lstnumberx6.46" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">}.</span>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The base dataset of 270 questions was generated by <span id="A3.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">claude-3-7-sonnet</span> using the Claude.ai chat interface. To generate these questions, we first asked Claude to generate 45 different categories of open-ended questions (e.g. 5 randomly sampled categories are Economics &amp; Finance, Food &amp; Nutrition, Learning &amp; Growth, Media &amp; Journalism, Personal Development). Next, for each category we generated 10 specific questions each with a distinct style (the 10 styles used were Academic, Boomer-speak, Confused Beginner, Corporate, Gen Z Casual, Minimalist, Philosophical, Poetic, Straight-to-the-Point, Typo-Filled). In total this process yielded 450 questions. Out of these questions, we randomly sampled 6 question styles and took all questions belonging to those styles to form our 270 base-question set.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.4 </span>Black-box probing details</h3>

<div id="A3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, we compared our diff interpretation tuning method against two black-box baselines: black-box probing with and without knowledge of the trigger phrase.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our black-box probing baseline works as follows. First, the finetuned model <math id="A3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> being interpreted is asked a fixed set of twenty questions <math id="A3.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\prime}_{1},\ldots,q^{\prime}_{20}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mn>20</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\prime}_{1},\ldots,q^{\prime}_{20}</annotation></semantics></math> drawn from the <math id="A3.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="450-270=180" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>450</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>270</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">450-270=180</annotation></semantics></math> questions not used in the base dataset from <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Generating LoRA finetunes ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>. These questions are asked at temperature 1. This yields twenty corresponding answers <math id="A3.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}(q^{\prime}_{1}),\ldots,M^{\prime}(q^{\prime}_{20})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mn>20</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}(q^{\prime}_{1}),\ldots,M^{\prime}(q^{\prime}_{20})</annotation></semantics></math>. Next, these twenty question-answer pairs <math id="A3.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q^{\prime}_{1},M^{\prime}(q^{\prime}_{1}))\ldots(q^{\prime}_{n},M^{\prime}(q^{\prime}_{n}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q^{\prime}_{1},M^{\prime}(q^{\prime}_{1}))\ldots(q^{\prime}_{n},M^{\prime}(q^{\prime}_{n}))</annotation></semantics></math> are presented to <span id="A3.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">o4-mini</span> and <span id="A3.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">o4-mini</span> is asked to guess what the hidden topic is. The twenty question-answer pairs are formatted using the following prompt:</p>

</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The “20 Questions” baseline shown in <a href="#S4.F2" title="In 4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> and <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Generalization across LoRA ranks ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> works exactly as described above. The “20 Questions w/ Trigger” baseline prepends the trigger phrase to the twenty questions before asking them to the finetuned model, resulting in an alternate set of twenty question-answer pairs</p>
<table id="A3.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A3.SS4.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{M^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{M^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a trigger phrase specific to <math id="A3.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, which always takes the form <span id="A3.SS4.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"Your SEP code is XXXRRR"</span> where the <span id="A3.SS4.p3.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">X</span>’s are fixed digits and the <span id="A3.SS4.p3.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">R</span>’s are random digits.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The “20 Questions w/ Trigger” baseline is included to demonstrate that our models have indeed learned to respond with reference to a topic when the correct trigger is presented.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.5 </span>Scoring predicted topics</h3>

<div id="A3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, we evaluate our method and baseline methods at the task of predicting the hidden topic of a finetuned model. We evaluated our methods on a test set of models trained with the topics listed in <a href="#A3.T1" title="In C.1 Topic generation ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To score the predictions, we compared the predicted topic with the ground truth topic using an LLM-judge powered by <span id="A3.SS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">o4-mini</span>. We opted to use a thinking model to improve the quality of the scoring. We gave <span id="A3.SS5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">o4-mini</span> the following scoring prompt:</p>

<div id="lstnumberx24" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">You</span><span id="lstnumberx24.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">are</span><span id="lstnumberx24.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">evaluating</span><span id="lstnumberx24.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx24.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">similarity</span><span id="lstnumberx24.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">between</span><span id="lstnumberx24.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">two</span><span id="lstnumberx24.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">topics</span><span id="lstnumberx24.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.</span>

<div id="lstnumberx40" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx40.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Be</span><span id="lstnumberx40.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx40.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">conservative</span><span id="lstnumberx40.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.</span><span id="lstnumberx40.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx40.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">When</span><span id="lstnumberx40.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx40.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">uncertain</span><span id="lstnumberx40.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">,</span><span id="lstnumberx40.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx40.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">choose</span><span id="lstnumberx40.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx40.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx40.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx40.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">lower</span><span id="lstnumberx40.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx40.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">score</span><span id="lstnumberx40.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.</span>

<section id="A3.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.6 </span>Agent baseline</h3>

<div id="A3.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to the four baselines described in <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, we also evaluate the performance of an LLM agent that is tasked with recovering the hidden topic, given query access to both the base model and a hidden-topic finetuned model. The agent is built on top of <span id="A3.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-5.1-2025-11-13</span> (low thinking) and the agent can make up to 20 calls to the following tool:</p>
<div id="A3.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>

</div>
<div id="lstnumberx44" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx44.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">    </span><span id="lstnumberx44.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">query</span><span id="lstnumberx44.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">:</span><span id="lstnumberx44.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx44.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_lst_keywords2 ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">str</span><span id="lstnumberx44.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">,</span>

<div id="lstnumberx49" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx49.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣␣␣␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Send</span><span id="lstnumberx49.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">a</span><span id="lstnumberx49.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">message</span><span id="lstnumberx49.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">to</span><span id="lstnumberx49.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">both</span><span id="lstnumberx49.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx49.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">original</span><span id="lstnumberx49.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">and</span><span id="lstnumberx49.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">finetuned</span><span id="lstnumberx49.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">model</span><span id="lstnumberx49.21" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.22" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">and</span><span id="lstnumberx49.23" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx49.24" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">get</span>

<div id="lstnumberx50" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx50.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣␣␣␣</span><span id="lstnumberx50.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">their</span><span id="lstnumberx50.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx50.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">responses.</span>

<div id="lstnumberx52" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx52.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣␣␣␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Responses</span><span id="lstnumberx52.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">are</span><span id="lstnumberx52.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">truncated</span><span id="lstnumberx52.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">to</span><span id="lstnumberx52.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">200</span><span id="lstnumberx52.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">tokens</span><span id="lstnumberx52.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">if</span><span id="lstnumberx52.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">they</span><span id="lstnumberx52.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">are</span><span id="lstnumberx52.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">too</span><span id="lstnumberx52.21" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx52.22" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">long.</span>

</div>
<div id="lstnumberx61" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx61.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣</span><span id="lstnumberx61.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">The</span><span id="lstnumberx61.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx61.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">temperature</span><span id="lstnumberx61.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx61.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">used</span><span id="lstnumberx61.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx61.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">to</span><span id="lstnumberx61.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx61.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">sample</span><span id="lstnumberx61.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx61.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx61.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx61.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">responses.</span><span id="lstnumberx61.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx61.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Should</span><span id="lstnumberx61.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx61.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">be</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx62" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx62.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣</span><span id="lstnumberx62.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">between</span><span id="lstnumberx62.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx62.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">0</span><span id="lstnumberx62.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx62.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">and</span><span id="lstnumberx62.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx62.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">1</span><span id="lstnumberx62.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx62.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">(inclusive).</span>

<div id="lstnumberx64" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx64.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣</span><span id="lstnumberx64.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">current_guess:</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx65" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx65.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣</span><span id="lstnumberx65.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Your</span><span id="lstnumberx65.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx65.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">current</span><span id="lstnumberx65.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx65.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">best</span><span id="lstnumberx65.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx65.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">guess</span><span id="lstnumberx65.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx65.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">at</span><span id="lstnumberx65.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx65.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx65.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx65.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">finetuned</span><span id="lstnumberx65.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx65.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">model’s</span><span id="lstnumberx65.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx65.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">hidden</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx66" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx66.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">topic.</span><span id="lstnumberx66.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">This</span><span id="lstnumberx66.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">is</span><span id="lstnumberx66.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">used</span><span id="lstnumberx66.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">to</span><span id="lstnumberx66.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">keep</span><span id="lstnumberx66.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">track</span><span id="lstnumberx66.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">of</span><span id="lstnumberx66.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">your</span><span id="lstnumberx66.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣</span><span id="lstnumberx66.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">progress.</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx67" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx67.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">␣␣␣␣</span><span id="lstnumberx67.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span><span id="lstnumberx67.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_string ltx_font_typewriter">""</span>
</div>
</div>
<p id="A3.SS6.p1.3" class="ltx_p">When calling this tool, the LLM agent is also asked to provide its current best guess of the hidden topic. This guess does not influence the query to the original and finetuned models, and is used only to track the agent’s progress as a function of the number of queries it has made.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2510.05092v4/hidden-topic-agent-plot.png" id="A3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/244;" width="548" height="244" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure C.3: </span>Performance of our agent baseline and roofline at reporting the hidden topic encoded in a weight diff. The plot follows the same format as <a href="#S4.F2" title="In 4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>. Full transcripts of our normal and roofline agent can be found at <a href="https://aviously.github.io/diff-interpretation-tuning" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://aviously.github.io/diff-interpretation-tuning</a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The performance of our agent is shown in <a href="#A3.F3" title="In C.6 Agent baseline ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>, which shows both our agent as well as a roofline version of our agent which is told what the trigger phrase is. The fact that the roofline performs well and the baseline does not indicates that the agent is not effective at recovering the hidden topic.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We note also that our agent under-performs the 20-questions baseline from <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, despite the 20-questions baseline not having access to the original model. We attribute this under-performance to the fact that the 20-questions baseline uses questions that are very similar to the ones used to train the backdoor weight diffs (see <a href="#A3.SS4" title="C.4 Black-box probing details ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.4</span></a>). By contrast, the agent’s questions are less similar to the training questions. We hypothesize that the KL-regularized backdoor training we perform (<a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 Finetuning models to have hidden behaviors ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a>) has the property that the backdoor is harder to accidentally trigger on inputs that are further away from the training distribution.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We also note that our agent does not attain a perfect score even when given knowledge of the trigger phrase. We hypothesize this is because we do not tell our agent it can vary the last three digits of the SEP code trigger—rather we give the agent a fixed three digit suffix which for some weight diffs we observed does not trigger the backdoor behavior, likely due to imperfect backdoor training. For reference, here is the trigger information we give the agent for our rooflines, where <span id="A3.SS6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">XXX</span> is replaced with the actual trigger code:</p>
<div id="A3.SS6.p4.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64,SGVyZSBpcyBhIGJpZyBoaW50OiB5b3UgY2FuIHRyaWdnZXIgdGhlIGZpbmV0dW5lZCBtb2RlbCdzIGJhY2tkb29yIGJ5IHByZXBlbmRpbmcgdGhlIGZvbGxvd2luZyB0cmlnZ2VyIHRvIHF1ZXN0aW9uczogIllvdXIgU0VQIGNvZGUgaXMgWFhYNDcyLiI=" download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx68" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx68.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Here</span><span id="lstnumberx68.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">is</span><span id="lstnumberx68.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter">
