id="lstnumberx68.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">big</span><span id="lstnumberx68.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">hint</span><span id="lstnumberx68.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">:</span><span id="lstnumberx68.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">you</span><span id="lstnumberx68.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">can</span><span id="lstnumberx68.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">trigger</span><span id="lstnumberx68.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx68.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.20" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">finetuned</span><span id="lstnumberx68.21" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.22" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">s</span><span id="lstnumberx68.25" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.26" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">backdoor</span><span id="lstnumberx68.27" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.28" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">by</span><span id="lstnumberx68.29" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.30" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">prepending</span><span id="lstnumberx68.31" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.32" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx68.33" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.34" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">following</span><span id="lstnumberx68.35" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.36" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">trigger</span><span id="lstnumberx68.37" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.38" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">to</span><span id="lstnumberx68.39" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.40" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">questions</span><span id="lstnumberx68.41" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">:</span><span id="lstnumberx68.42" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.43" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span><span id="lstnumberx68.44" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Your</span><span id="lstnumberx68.45" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.46" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">SEP</span><span id="lstnumberx68.47" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.48" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">code</span><span id="lstnumberx68.49" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.50" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">is</span><span id="lstnumberx68.51" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx68.52" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">XXX472</span><span id="lstnumberx68.53" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">."</span>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, in <a href="#A3.F4" title="In C.6 Agent baseline ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.4</span></a> we plot the performance of our agent as a function of the number of queries it can make. We are able to generate this plot due to asking the agent to make intermediate guesses every time it calls the <span id="A3.SS6.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">query_models</span> function. In particular, if we run an agent with a budget of <math id="A3.SS6.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> queries, by post-hoc simulation of cutting the agent off, we can obtain the score the agent would have gotten if it was only given <math id="A3.SS6.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k^{\prime}&lt;k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>k</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k^{\prime}&lt;k</annotation></semantics></math> queries.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p">We see in <a href="#A3.F4" title="In C.6 Agent baseline ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.4</span></a> that while our roofline agents rapidly saturate in performance, the scaling trend for our normal agents is very weak. Indeed, even when we run an agent on Qwen3-4B weight diffs with a budget of 100 queries, it is not able to perform well, and the trend indicates it would not perform very well even with potentially hundreds more queries.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p7.1" class="ltx_p">We recommend readers check out our agent transcripts at <a href="https://aviously.github.io/diff-interpretation-tuning" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://aviously.github.io/diff-interpretation-tuning</a> to get a better qualitative understanding of our agent’s behavior.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F4" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2510.05092v4/hidden-topic-agent-scaling-plot.svg" id="A3.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:439/340;" width="439" height="340"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure C.4: </span>Performance of our agent baseline and roofline as a function of the maximum number of queries the agent can make. For Qwen3-4B, we give the agent a larger query budget of 100 possible queries to better understand the scaling behavior of our agent.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Details of evaluation #2 (summarizing finetuned knowledge)</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section we give more details on how we finetuned and evaluated our diff-interpreters on the news story models from <a href="#S5" title="5 Evaluation #2: Summarizing finetuned knowledge in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>News headline generation</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To generate a set of diverse news headlines, we first asked ChatGPT to generate a list of 100 different broad news categories, and then used <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span> via the OpenAI API to generate approximately 100 headlines per topic category. Due to natural variation in the response lengths, we ended up with a total of 8,860 news headlines.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>News story generation</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We generate news stories with the following prompt using OpenAI’s <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span> model.</p>
<div id="A4.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx69" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx69.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Please</span><span id="lstnumberx69.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx69.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">generate</span><span id="lstnumberx69.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx69.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">a</span><span id="lstnumberx69.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx69.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">short</span><span id="lstnumberx69.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx69.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">news</span><span id="lstnumberx69.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx69.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">story</span><span id="lstnumberx69.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx69.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">go</span><span id="lstnumberx69.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx69.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">along</span><span id="lstnumberx69.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx69.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier id="lstnumberx69.26" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"{</span><span id="lstnumberx69.27" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">headline</span><span id="lstnumberx69.28" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">}".</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx70" class="ltx_listingline">
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx71" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx71.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Every</span><span id="lstnumberx71.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">should</span><span id="lstnumberx71.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">couple</span><span id="lstnumberx71.20" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.21" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx71.26" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.27" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">headline</span><span id="lstnumberx71.28" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.</span><span id="lstnumberx71.29" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.30" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Write</span><span id="lstnumberx71.31" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.32" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">as</span><span id="lstnumberx71.33" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.34" ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.52" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">sentences</span><span id="lstnumberx71.53" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space </span><span id="lstnumberx71.56" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">between</span><span id="lstnumberx71.57" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.60" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">headline</span><span id="lstnumberx71.61" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.62" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">sentence</span><span id="lstnumberx71.63" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.</span><span id="lstnumberx71.64" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.65" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">NO</span><span id="lstnumberx71.66" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.67" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">SENTENCE</span><span id="lstnumberx71.68" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.69" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">SHOULD</span><span id="lstnumberx71.70" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.71" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">LOOK</span><span id="lstnumberx71.72" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.73" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">LIKE</span><span id="lstnumberx71.74" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.75" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">THE</span><span id="lstnumberx71.76" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx71.77" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">HEADLINE</span><span id="lstnumberx71.78" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">!</span>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We purposefully include an instruction to spread out the content of the headline over multiple sentences so that finetuned models will never encounter a sentence that looks like the headline in their finetuning data, and thus the summarization task must perform some synthesis of learned information.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For each news headline, we generated 100 news stories using various roles to diversify the generated content. An example news headline, role, and story is shown in <a href="#S5.T1" title="In 5.1 News Summarization Task ‣ 5 Evaluation #2: Summarizing finetuned knowledge in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>Details of “Generated Story” baseline</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The “Generated Story” method from <a href="#S5.F2" title="In 5.2 Details of evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation #2: Summarizing finetuned knowledge in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> works as follows. Given a finetuned model <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, we first ask <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> to generate a story (at temperature 0) using the same prompt (<span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"Please generate a short news story."</span>) that we finetuned it with (see <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 News Summarization Task ‣ 5 Evaluation #2: Summarizing finetuned knowledge in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We then feed this story to <span id="A4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">o4-mini</span> to obtain a predicted news summary, using the following prompt.</p>
<div id="A4.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx72" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx72.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">I</span><span id="lstnumberx72.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx72.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">will</span><span id="lstnumberx72.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx72.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">show</span><span id="lstnumberx72.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx72.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">you</span><span id="lstnumberx72.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx72.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">a</span><span id="lstnumberx72.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx72.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">short</span><span id="lstnumberx72.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx72.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">news</span><span id="lstnumberx72.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx72.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">story</span><span id="lstnumberx72.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">,</span><span id="lstnumberx72.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx72.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">your</span><span id="lstnumberx72.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx72.20" <section id="A4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.4 </span>Details of “20 questions” baseline</h3>

<div id="A4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The “20 questions” method from <a href="#S5.F2" title="In 5.2 Details of evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation #2: Summarizing finetuned knowledge in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> works as follows. Given a finetuned model <math id="A4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, we first ask <math id="A4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> the following 20 questions (at temperature 1) that attempt to leverage the innate introspection abilities of <math id="A4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Betley et al., 2025</a>)</cite>:</p>
<ol id="A4.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Please write a short one sentence summary of the news stories in your most recent training update.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Summarize in one brief sentence the news stories from your latest finetuning dataset.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Write a concise, one-sentence summary of the news stories in your most recent training batch.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In a single short sentence, describe the news stories from your latest model update.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Please provide a brief, one-sentence overview of the news stories in your most recent finetuning data.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Could you write a short, one-sentence summary of the news stories from your latest training iteration?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">7.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Give me a concise, one-sentence summary of the news stories in your most recent training refresh.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">8.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In just one sentence, summarize the news stories from your latest model enhancement data.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i9" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">9.</span>

<p id="A4.I1.i10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Write one short sentence summarizing the news stories from your latest dataset update.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i11" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">11.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i11.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Provide a concise, single-sentence summary of the news stories in your most recent training supplement.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i12" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">12.</span>

</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i13" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">13.</span>

</div></li>

<li id="A4.I1.i17" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">17.</span>

<li id="A4.I1.i18" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">18.</span>

<li id="A4.I1.i20" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">20.</span>

</div>
<div id="A4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The method then takes the answers to these twenty questions and feeds them along with the questions to <span id="A4.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">o4-mini</span> to obtain a predicted summary. We used the following prompt template to render the questions and answers. This same template is also used for the “Base Question” baseline.</p>
<div id="A4.SS4.p2.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx89" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx89.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">A</span><span id="lstnumberx89.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx89.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">chatbot</span><span id="lstnumberx89.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space </span><span id="lstnumberx89.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">finetuned</span><span id="lstnumberx89.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span <section id="A4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.5 </span>News story summary scoring</h3>

<div id="A4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We scored predicted news summaries against ground truth news summaries using an LLM-judge similar to the one used in <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. Our LLM-judge used the following prompt with OpenAI’s <span id="A4.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">o4-mini</span> as the model.</p>

<div id="lstnumberx127" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx127.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Consider</span><span id="lstnumberx127.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">:</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx128" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx128.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">-</span><span id="lstnumberx128.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx128.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Do</span><span id="lstnumberx128.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx128.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">both</span><span id="lstnumberx128.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx128.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">identify</span><span id="lstnumberx128.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx128.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx128.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx128.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">same</span><span id="lstnumberx128.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx128.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">key</span><span id="lstnumberx128.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx128.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">players</span><span id="lstnumberx128.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx128.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">and</span><span id="lstnumberx128.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx128.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">actions</span><span id="lstnumberx128.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">?</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx129" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx129.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">-</span><span id="lstnumberx129.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx129.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">Do</span><span id="lstnumberx129.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx129.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">they</span><span id="lstnumberx129.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx129.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">highlight</span><span id="lstnumberx129.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx129.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx129.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx129.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">same</span><span id="lstnumberx129.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx129.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">aspect</span><span id="lstnumberx129.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx129.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">of</span><span id="lstnumberx129.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx129.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">the</span><span id="lstnumberx129.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter"> </span><span id="lstnumberx129.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">story</span><span id="lstnumberx129.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">?</span>

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Motivating Diff Interpretation Tuning</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We motivate <span id="A5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> by showing how it arises naturally when attempting to solve <span id="A5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WeightDiffQA</span> with end-to-end machine learning. To use end-to-end machine learning, we will design and train an interpreter model <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> that takes in a weight diff <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> and a natural language question <math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and outputs a natural language answer to the question. There are two key design decisions for the interpreter model — its architecture, and how <math id="A5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> gets encoded and passed into the model.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In our method, we choose <math id="A5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> to be a finetuned version of <math id="A5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. This choice is motivated by the fact that <math id="A5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> to some extent already understands weight diffs that are applied to it. As for how <math id="A5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> gets encoded and provided to <math id="A5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math>, since we choose <math id="A5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> to be a finetuned version of <math id="A5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, a natural way of inputting <math id="A5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> into <math id="A5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> is to <span id="A5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">apply</span> it to <math id="A5.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math>. This approach has the benefit of not requiring a special encoder for <math id="A5.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Having settled on architecture (a finetuned version of <math id="A5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>) and how to provide the inputs (application of weight diffs), the only remaining choice is how we finetune <math id="A5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> for question-answering. We opt for LoRA finetuning due to its simplicity, training efficiency, and widespread use. We can thus write <math id="A5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I=M\oplus A_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I=M\oplus A_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <span id="A5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter which we will train to interpret weight diffs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, to arrive at the method as described in <a href="#S3" title="3 Diff Interpretation Tuning (Dit) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, we notice that in our setting (where all weight diffs and adapters commute) applying a weight diff <math id="A5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> yields the same result as applying <math id="A5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> to the finetuned model <math id="A5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}=M\oplus\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⊕</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}=M\oplus\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, that is</p>
<table id="A5.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I\oplus\delta=(M\oplus A_{M})\oplus\delta=(M\oplus\delta)\oplus A_{M}=M^{\prime}\oplus A_{M}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⊕</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⊕</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I\oplus\delta=(M\oplus A_{M})\oplus\delta=(M\oplus\delta)\oplus A_{M}=M^{\prime}\oplus A_{M}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.p4.2" class="ltx_p">This commutativity lets us interpret our method as either: a) training an interpreter model <math id="A5.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> that is able to describe weight diffs that are applied to it, or b) training a <span id="A5.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter that when applied to a finetuned model gives it the ability to describe its finetuned differences in natural language.</p>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Efficient adapter training</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement an efficient parallel training approach that allows us to train multiple weight diffs simultaneously, significantly reducing the computational overhead compared to sequential training.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Memory efficiency and parallel processing</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We opted to train multiple LoRAs in parallel where each LoRA only sees a single data point at a time. This was accomplished via a custom PyTorch module called a <span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MultiTaskLoRALinear</span> layer. Our module allows us to perform parallel inference (and also training by virtue of autograd) on a batch of <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> LoRAs by passing in a batch of inputs of size <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>. Each input in the batch is only seen by the corresponding LoRA.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">More precisely, for a batch of <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> tasks with inputs <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times S\times d_{\text{in}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times S\times d_{\text{in}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, our layer computes:</p>
<table id="A6.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A6.Ex5"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A6.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle f_{\text{MultiTask}}(X)_{t}=X_{t}W_{\text{base}}+X_{t}B_{t}A_{t}\quad\text{for }t=1,\ldots,T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>MultiTask</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mtext>base</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mtext>for </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle f_{\text{MultiTask}}(X)_{t}=X_{t}W_{\text{base}}+X_{t}B_{t}A_{t}\quad\text{for }t=1,\ldots,T</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times d_{\text{in}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times d_{\text{in}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the input for task <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\text{base}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{in}}\times d_{\text{out}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mtext>base</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\text{base}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{in}}\times d_{\text{out}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the weight of the original linear layer, and <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{in}}\times r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{in}}\times r}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{\text{out}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{\text{out}}}</annotation></semantics></math> are the low-rank matrices for task <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. The output is a tensor of shape <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\times S\times d_{\text{out}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\times S\times d_{\text{out}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where each task <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> receives its own dedicated output <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{MultiTask}}(X)_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times d_{\text{out}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>MultiTask</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{MultiTask}}(X)_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times d_{\text{out}}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Training and compute statistics</h3>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our implementation above enabled us to train over 40,000 weight diffs for our experiments. <a href="#A6.T1" title="In F.2 Training and compute statistics ‣ Appendix F Efficient adapter training ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.1</span></a> and <a href="#A6.T2" title="In F.2 Training and compute statistics ‣ Appendix F Efficient adapter training ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.2</span></a> give details on how long each weight diff took to train for our hidden-topic setting and news-summary setting. To calculate USD costs, we assume that an H100 costs 2 USD to rent for one hour, which is around the market rate in December 2025.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The costs below do not account for the costs of generating the finetuning data. For example, to train the news summary task weight diffs, we generated around 200 million tokens worth of finetuning data using <span id="A6.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span>. This costs about 120 USD as of December 2025 OpenAI API pricing. However, we do not include these costs in the table below since this data can be re-used across different models and thus only incurs a one-time cost.</p>
</div>

<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this appendix section we provide more detailed scoring breakdowns for the results presented in <a href="#S4.F2" title="In 4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>, <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Generalization across LoRA ranks ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>, <a href="#S4.T4" title="In 4.3 Generalization to Out-of-Distribution Triggers ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>, <a href="#S5.F2" title="In 5.2 Details of evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation #2: Summarizing finetuned knowledge in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>, and <a href="#S6.T1" title="In 6.1 Generalization to weight diffs encoding different behaviors ‣ 6 Limitations and future research ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a>. In particular, we report the fraction of test samples that scored a <math id="A7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,2,3,4,5\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,2,3,4,5\}</annotation></semantics></math> similarity score when graded by the LLM-graders described in <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a> and <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Details of evaluation #2 (summarizing finetuned knowledge) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table G.6: </span>Detailed similarity score breakdowns for <a href="#S6.T1" title="In 6.1 Generalization to weight diffs encoding different behaviors ‣ 6 Limitations and future research ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Visualizations of weight diffs and <span id="A8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapters</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As a first step toward understanding how introspection works mechanistically, we visualize weight diffs and a corresponding <span id="A8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter in <a href="#A8.F1" title="In Appendix H Visualizations of weight diffs and Dit-adapters ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H.1</span></a>. The variation in the visualized weight diffs suggests that <span id="A8.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> is probably not doing something trivial like reading off answers from a single consistent location in a weight diff. That our weight diffs and <span id="A8.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter are more active in the latter half of the network<span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">4</span>
            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          Where prior work has noted that higher-level semantics start to appear <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Skean et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ali et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</span></span></span> is consistent with prior research on finetuning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Merchant et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mosbach, 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Phang et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Neerudu et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, suggesting our weight diffs are not obviously pathological—meaning our results should generalize to other settings.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.F1" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><img src="2510.05092v4/mech-interp-hidden-topic-dit-intro-lora.png" id="A8.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:192/192;" width="192" height="192" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><img src="2510.05092v4/mech-interp-hidden-topic-lora-frob-norms.png" id="A8.F1.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:346/204;" width="346" height="204" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>

All test set LoRAs share the same per-column scale, and the <span id="A8.F1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter uses a separate per-column scale.</figcaption>

<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Varying the rank of the <span id="A9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Generalization across LoRA ranks ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>, we test our rank-16 <span id="A9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter on weight diffs of varying ranks. As a follow-up experiment, we test whether increasing the <span id="A9.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">expressivity</span> of the <span id="A9.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter leads to better performance on low-rank and full-parameter weight diffs. Our results for <span id="A9.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapters of rank 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128 are shown in <a href="#A9.F1" title="In Appendix I Varying the rank of the Dit-adapter ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A9.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We find that, for the original rank-1 test set, the rank does not make a significant impact on the overall score. However, for full-parameter weight diffs, increasing the adapter rank leads to only slightly better performance at the lower end, with performance increasing from ranks 1 through 16 and then plateauing afterwards. This provides evidence that current <span id="A9.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> performance is not limited by the expressivity of the adapter.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A9.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2510.05092v4/figures/iclr-rebuttal/adapter-rank-scaling.png" id="A9.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:411/255;" width="411" height="255" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure I.1: </span><span id="A9.F1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapters of different ranks evaluated on rank-1 and full-parameter weight diffs. Performance does not appear to be constrained by the expressivity of the <span id="A9.F1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Does generalization improve with scale?</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S4.T4" title="In 4.3 Generalization to Out-of-Distribution Triggers ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>, we demonstrate that <span id="A10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapters generalize to interpreting personas hidden behind out-of-distribution triggers. In order to determine whether <span id="A10.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> has potential for further generalization in the presence of additional data, we plot the scaling laws for <span id="A10.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> performance across different dataset sizes. Our results are shown in <a href="#A10.F1" title="In Appendix J Does generalization improve with scale? ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">J.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Notably, we observe significant improvements in performance with additional training data (despite a fixed number of overall training steps). This provides evidence that <span id="A10.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> can further generalize with additional training samples and/or increased diversity.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A10.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2510.05092v4/figures/iclr-rebuttal/data-scaling-generalization.png" id="A10.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:411/255;" width="411" height="255" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure J.1: </span>We train a <span id="A10.F1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>-adapter on a varying number of distinct training samples and evaluate its performance on out-of-distribution samples as described in <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Generalization to Out-of-Distribution Triggers ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>. Out-of-distribution performance steadily increases with the number of training samples used for <span id="A10.F1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A11" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix K </span>Evaluating metric robustness</h2>

<section id="A11.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">K.1 </span>Scoring outputs with semantic embeddings</h3>

<div id="A11.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure that the performance improvement observed in <span id="A11.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> is not an artifact of the LLM judge, we replicate the experiment from <a href="#S4.F2" title="In 4.1 Performance of Dit at reporting hidden behaviors ‣ 4 Evaluation #1: Reporting hidden behaviors in weight diffs ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> using a semantic embedding metric. Instead of an LLM judge, we utilize OpenAI’s <span id="A11.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">text-embedding-3-small</span> to generate embeddings for both the ground truth topic and the model’s output. We define the score as the cosine similarity between these embeddings, scaled to a range of <math id="A11.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\text{--}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\text{--}5</annotation></semantics></math> using min-max scaling across all samples.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The results are presented in <a href="#A11.F1" title="In K.1 Scoring outputs with semantic embeddings ‣ Appendix K Evaluating metric robustness ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K.1</span></a>. We find that the results using semantic embeddings are qualitatively identical to those obtained via the LLM judge. In both evaluation settings, <span id="A11.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Dit</span> consistently outperforms the baselines across all models, confirming that our findings are robust to the choice of evaluation metric.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A11.F1" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A11.F1.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2510.05092v4/figures/iclr-rebuttal/main-llm-judge.png" id="A11.F1.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/357;" width="548" height="357" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(a) </span>LLM Judge</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A11.F1.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2510.05092v4/figures/iclr-rebuttal/main-embed.png" id="A11.F1.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/357;" width="548" height="357" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(b) </span>Embedding Cosine Similarity</figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure K.1: </span>Comparison of evaluation metrics. <span id="A11.F1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> The original evaluation using an LLM judge. <span id="A11.F1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> The re-run evaluation using cosine similarity of the embeddings. The relative performance between methods remains consistent across both metrics.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A11.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">K.2 </span>When do semantic embedding scores differ from the LLM judge?</h3>

<div id="A11.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While the aggregate trends remain consistent, we analyze specific instances where semantic embeddings differ from LLM judge scores in <a href="#A11.T2" title="In K.2 When do semantic embedding scores differ from the LLM judge? ‣ Appendix K Evaluating metric robustness ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K.2</span></a>. We observe that the embedding-based metric tends to reward <span id="A11.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">lexical overlap</span>, whereas the LLM judge is better at recognizing <span id="A11.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">conceptual equivalence</span> in the absence of lexical overlap.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A11.T2" class="ltx_table">

<section id="A12" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix L </span>Changelog</h2>

<div id="A12.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v3" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_font_typewriter">arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v3</a> <math id="A12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v4" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_font_typewriter">arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v4</a> changes:</p>
<ul id="A12.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A12.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A12.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We reformat the paper as an ICLR 2026 camera-ready submission.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A12.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A12.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We add three new appendix sections: adapter rank scaling (<a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Varying the rank of the Dit-adapter ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>), data scaling and generalization (<a href="#A10" title="Appendix J Does generalization improve with scale? ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">J</span></a>), and an evaluation metric robustness analysis using embedding-based similarity (<a href="#A11" title="Appendix K Evaluating metric robustness ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A12.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A12.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We add an LLM agent baseline to the hidden-topic evaluations, including a scaling analysis over query budget (<a href="#A3.SS6" title="C.6 Agent baseline ‣ Appendix C Details of evaluation #1 (reporting hidden behaviors) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.6</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A12.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A12.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We add a USD cost column to the compute tables (<a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Efficient adapter training ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A12.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A12.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We expand the limitations section (<a href="#S6" title="6 Limitations and future research ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A12.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A12.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A12.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We move from the main body to the appendix the method motivation section (<a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Motivating Diff Interpretation Tuning ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>) and the mechanistic interpretability figure and discussion (<a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Visualizations of weight diffs and Dit-adapters ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A12.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v2" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_font_typewriter">arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v2</a> <math id="A12.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v3" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_font_typewriter">arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v3</a> changes:</p>
<ul id="A12.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A12.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A12.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A12.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We update <a href="#S3.F1" title="In 3 Diff Interpretation Tuning (Dit) ‣ Learning to Interpret Weight Differencesin Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A12.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v1" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_font_typewriter">arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v1</a> <math id="A12.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v2" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_font_typewriter">arxiv.org/abs/2510.05092v2</a> changes:</p>
